notes: The app no longer claims a song is playing when it is not. When the screen goes off or you leave the app, Android freezes the WebView and the audio dies with it — while the player still reported “playing”, with a playhead that never moved. The app now compares the real playhead against the time actually spent away, so it can tell a song that survived the trip from one that was silently killed

When the audio was killed in the background, the song is put back where it left off as soon as you return — you no longer have to press play. If the system refuses to restart without a tap, the app shows an honest paused state instead of a playing display over silence

The app never reloads itself into a staged update any more. That automatic hand-over (on launch, and on the way out of the app) is what made the app “refresh by itself” when you opened it — and the refresh landed on top of playback, so the song was gone. Updates now wait for the native updater to install them on a real app close/relaunch, and the sheet offers to install one on the spot
An update staged while a song is playing is handed to the updater with a “when the app is closed” condition, so it can no longer swap itself in under a playing song
Every background stall is recorded on the device (tap the version label in Settings five times to see it), so if a song still stops the reason is on screen instead of guessed at
